informal_statement:
All graphs below are finite, simple, and undirected. An independent set in a graph is a vertex set whose distinct vertices are pairwise nonadjacent. Write α(G[X]) for the maximum size of an independent set contained in X, with α(G[∅]) = 0. For positive integers a and b, K_{a,b} is the complete bipartite graph with independent parts of sizes a and b and every possible edge between the parts. A graph is induced K_{a,b}-free if no vertex subset induces a graph isomorphic to K_{a,b}.

A tree decomposition of G consists of a finite nonempty tree T and a bag β(x) ⊆ V(G) for each node x of T, such that the bags cover V(G), both ends of every edge of G belong to a common bag, and for each vertex v of G the nodes whose bags contain v induce a nonempty connected subtree of T. Its independence number is max_{x ∈ V(T)} α(G[β(x)]). The tree-independence number tree-α(G) is the minimum of these numbers over all tree decompositions of G.

An induced matching in G is a set of vertex-disjoint edges such that the subgraph induced by all their endpoints has exactly those edges. For |V(G)| ≥ 2, a branch decomposition of G consists of a finite tree T whose non-leaf nodes all have degree three and a bijection φ from V(G) to the leaves of T. Deleting an edge e of T partitions its leaves into two components and hence partitions V(G) into sets A_e and B_e. The sim-value of this cut is the maximum size of an induced matching in the whole graph G all of whose edges have one endpoint in A_e and the other in B_e. The width of the branch decomposition is the maximum sim-value over edges of T. The sim-width simw(G) is the minimum such width over all branch decompositions; set simw(G) = 0 when |V(G)| ≤ 1.

For every pair of positive integers a and b and every nonnegative integer s, there exists a nonnegative integer k such that every finite simple graph G that is induced K_{a,b}-free and satisfies simw(G) ≤ s also satisfies tree-α(G) ≤ k.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def ALIndependent {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ I, ∀ v ∈ I, u ≠ v → ¬ G.Adj u v

def ALInducedBicliqueFree {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (A B : Finset (Fin n)),
    A.card = a ∧ B.card = b ∧ Disjoint A B ∧
    ALIndependent G A ∧ ALIndependent G B ∧
    (∀ u ∈ A, ∀ v ∈ B, G.Adj u v)

def ALDeletedAdj {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (x y u v : Fin m) : Prop :=
  T.Adj u v ∧ ¬ ((u = x ∧ v = y) ∨ (u = y ∧ v = x))

def ALTree (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) : Prop :=
  0 < m ∧
  (∀ x y : Fin m, Relation.ReflTransGen T.Adj x y) ∧
  (∀ x y : Fin m, T.Adj x y →
    ¬ Relation.ReflTransGen (ALDeletedAdj T x y) x y)

noncomputable def ALDegree {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (x : Fin m) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (fun y : Fin m => T.Adj x y)).card

def ALTreeDecomposition {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (bag : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ALTree m T ∧
  (∀ v : Fin n, ∃ x : Fin m, v ∈ bag x) ∧
  (∀ u v : Fin n, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ x : Fin m, u ∈ bag x ∧ v ∈ bag x) ∧
  (∀ (v : Fin n) (x y : Fin m),
    v ∈ bag x → v ∈ bag y →
    Relation.ReflTransGen
      (fun p q : Fin m => T.Adj p q ∧ v ∈ bag p ∧ v ∈ bag q) x y)

def ALTreeAlphaLE {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
      (bag : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
    ALTreeDecomposition G m T bag ∧
    (∀ (x : Fin m) (I : Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ v ∈ I, v ∈ bag x) → ALIndependent G I → I.card ≤ k)

def ALInducedMatching {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (u v : Fin r → Fin n) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (Sum.elim u v : Sum (Fin r) (Fin r) → Fin n) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin r, G.Adj (u i) (v i)) ∧
  (∀ i j : Fin r, i ≠ j →
    ¬ G.Adj (u i) (u j) ∧
    ¬ G.Adj (v i) (v j) ∧
    ¬ G.Adj (u i) (v j))

def ALCutBound {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (A : Set (Fin n)) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (u v : Fin r → Fin n),
    ALInducedMatching G u v →
    (∀ i : Fin r,
      (u i ∈ A ∧ v i ∉ A) ∨ (v i ∈ A ∧ u i ∉ A)) →
    r ≤ s

def ALBranchDecomposition (n m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (φ : Fin n → Fin m) : Prop :=
  ALTree m T ∧
  (∀ x : Fin m, ALDegree T x = 1 ∨ ALDegree T x = 3) ∧
  Function.Injective φ ∧
  (∀ x : Fin m, (∃ v : Fin n, φ v = x) ↔ ALDegree T x = 1)

def ALCutSide {n m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (φ : Fin n → Fin m) (x y : Fin m) : Set (Fin n) :=
  {v | Relation.ReflTransGen (ALDeletedAdj T x y) x (φ v)}

def ALSimWidthLE {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  n ≤ 1 ∨
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (φ : Fin n → Fin m),
    ALBranchDecomposition n m T φ ∧
    (∀ x y : Fin m, T.Adj x y →
      ALCutBound G (ALCutSide T φ x y) s)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b →
  ∀ s : ℕ, ∃ k : ℕ,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ALInducedBicliqueFree G a b →
      ALSimWidthLE G s →
      ALTreeAlphaLE G k

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement: A standard Borel space is a measurable space measurably isomorphic to a Polish space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra; a Polish space is a separable topological space whose topology is induced by some complete metric. For every integer n ≥ 1, every standard Borel space X, every family of Borel measurable functions F₀, …, Fₙ₋₁ : X → X, and every probability measure μ on the Borel σ-algebra of X, define the undirected graph G on X by declaring distinct points x and y adjacent exactly when Fᵢ(x) = y or Fᵢ(y) = x for some i < n. There exists a function c : X → {0, 1, …, 2n} that is proper on all of X, meaning c(x) ≠ c(y) for every adjacent pair, and is measurable with respect to the μ-completion of the Borel σ-algebra. Explicitly, the latter condition means that for each color a there are Borel sets Bₐ and Nₐ with μ(Nₐ) = 0 such that the symmetric difference between c⁻¹({a}) and Bₐ is contained in Nₐ.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

universe u

def HasStandardBorelStructure (X : Type u) (m : MeasurableSpace X) : Prop :=
  ∃ t : TopologicalSpace X, @PolishSpace X t ∧ m = @borel X t

def FunctionGeneratedAdjacency {X : Type u} {n : ℕ}
    (F : Fin n → X → X) (x y : X) : Prop :=
  x ≠ y ∧ ∃ i : Fin n, F i x = y ∨ F i y = x

def TotalProperColoring {X : Type u} {n q : ℕ}
    (F : Fin n → X → X) (c : X → Fin q) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : X, FunctionGeneratedAdjacency F x y → c x ≠ c y

def CompletionMeasurableColoring {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X]
    {q : ℕ} (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure X) (c : X → Fin q) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : Fin q, ∃ B N : Set X,
    MeasurableSet B ∧ MeasurableSet N ∧ μ N = 0 ∧
      (({x : X | c x = a} \ B) ∪ (B \ {x : X | c x = a})) ⊆ N

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
  ∀ (X : Type u) (m : MeasurableSpace X),
    letI : MeasurableSpace X := m;
    HasStandardBorelStructure X m →
    ∀ (F : Fin n → X → X),
      (∀ i : Fin n, Measurable (F i)) →
      ∀ (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure X),
        MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        ∃ c : X → Fin (2 * n + 1),
          TotalProperColoring F c ∧ CompletionMeasurableColoring μ c

informal_statement: Let L be any at most countable complete lattice, where at most countable includes finite, and a complete lattice is a partially ordered set in which every subset has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound. Write x ∧ y for the greatest lower bound of x and y, and ⋁D for the least upper bound of a subset D. A subset D of L is directed if it is nonempty and, for every d₁,d₂ ∈ D, there is d₃ ∈ D with d₁ ≤ d₃ and d₂ ≤ d₃. Assume that L is meet-continuous: for every x ∈ L and every directed subset D ⊆ L, x ∧ ⋁D = ⋁{x ∧ d : d ∈ D}. Equip L with the Scott topology: a subset U ⊆ L is open precisely when it is an upper set (x ∈ U and x ≤ y imply y ∈ U) and, for every directed D ⊆ L, ⋁D ∈ U implies D ∩ U ≠ ∅. A set is closed if its complement is open. A nonempty closed set A is irreducible if, whenever two open sets U and V each meet A, their intersection U ∩ V also meets A. Is the Scott topology of every such L sober, meaning that every nonempty irreducible closed subset A is the closure of exactly one point q ∈ L? Here the closure of {q} is the intersection of all closed sets containing q; in the Scott topology it equals {x ∈ L : x ≤ q}.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def DirectedNonemptySubset (L : Type) [PartialOrder L] (D : Set L) : Prop :=
  D.Nonempty ∧
    ∀ a ∈ D, ∀ b ∈ D, ∃ c ∈ D, a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ c

def MeetContinuousProperty (L : Type) [CompleteLattice L] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : L, ∀ D : Set L, DirectedNonemptySubset L D →
    x ⊓ sSup D = sSup ((fun d : L => x ⊓ d) '' D)

def ScottOpenSubset (L : Type) [CompleteLattice L] (U : Set L) : Prop :=
  (∀ x ∈ U, ∀ y : L, x ≤ y → y ∈ U) ∧
    (∀ D : Set L, DirectedNonemptySubset L D →
      sSup D ∈ U → ∃ d ∈ D, d ∈ U)

def ScottClosedSubset (L : Type) [CompleteLattice L] (A : Set L) : Prop :=
  ScottOpenSubset L Aᶜ

def ScottIrreducibleSubset (L : Type) [CompleteLattice L] (A : Set L) : Prop :=
  A.Nonempty ∧
    ∀ U V : Set L,
      ScottOpenSubset L U → ScottOpenSubset L V →
      (A ∩ U).Nonempty → (A ∩ V).Nonempty →
      (A ∩ (U ∩ V)).Nonempty

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : Type) [CompleteLattice L] [Countable L],
  MeetContinuousProperty L →
    ∀ A : Set L,
      ScottClosedSubset L A → ScottIrreducibleSubset L A →
        ∃! q : L, A = {x : L | x ≤ q}

informal_statement:
For every integer n ≥ 1, let (Ω, F, μ) be a probability space and let X₁, …, Xₙ : Ω → ℝ be measurable random variables forming a centered Gaussian vector. This means that, for every a₁, …, aₙ ∈ ℝ, the random variable ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ aᵢXᵢ has a normal distribution with mean zero and some variance v ≥ 0: for v > 0 this distribution has density (2πv)⁻¹ᐟ² exp(−x²/(2v)), and for v = 0 it is the point mass at zero. No nonsingularity or independence assumption is imposed. Then, for every integer m ≥ 1,
Eμ[∏ᵢ₌₁ⁿ Xᵢ^(2m)] ≥ ∏ᵢ₌₁ⁿ Eμ[Xᵢ^(2m)],
where Eμ[Y] denotes the integral of Y with respect to μ.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators
open MeasureTheory

noncomputable def centeredNormalDensity (v x : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi * v))⁻¹ *
    Real.exp (-(x ^ 2) / (2 * v)))

noncomputable def IsCenteredGaussianFamily
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (n : ℕ)
    (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact
    (∀ i : Fin n, Measurable (X i)) ∧
    (∀ a : Fin n → ℝ, ∃ v : ℝ, 0 ≤ v ∧
      ∀ s : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet s →
        μ ((fun ω : Ω => ∑ i : Fin n, a i * X i ω) ⁻¹' s) =
          (if v = 0 then
            (if (0 : ℝ) ∈ s then 1 else 0)
          else
            ∫⁻ x in s, centeredNormalDensity v x
              ∂(MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)))

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
  ∀ (Ω : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω),
    MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
    ∀ X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ,
      IsCenteredGaussianFamily μ n X →
      ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m →
        (∏ i : Fin n, ∫ ω, (X i ω) ^ (2 * m) ∂μ) ≤
          ∫ ω, (∏ i : Fin n, (X i ω) ^ (2 * m)) ∂μ

informal_statement: For a positive integer n, a normalized Hadamard matrix of order n+1 is a real (n+1)×(n+1) matrix H, indexed by 0,1,…,n, whose entries belong to {−1,1}, whose zeroth row and zeroth column consist entirely of 1s, and which satisfies HᵀH=(n+1)I_{n+1}, where I_{n+1} is the identity matrix. An S-matrix of order n is a real n×n matrix S for which there exists such a normalized Hadamard matrix H with S_{ij}=(1−H_{ij})/2 for all 1≤i,j≤n. For a real n×n matrix B, define its Frobenius norm by ‖B‖_F=(∑_{i=1}^n∑_{j=1}^n B_{ij}²)^{1/2}. Is it true that, for every positive integer n and every real n×n matrix A=(a_{ij}) with det(A)≠0 and 0≤a_{ij}≤1 for all 1≤i,j≤n, the inverse matrix satisfies ‖A^{-1}‖_F≥2n/(n+1), with equality if and only if A is an S-matrix of order n?
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def designFrobeniusNorm (n : ℕ)
    (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, (B i j) ^ 2)

def designNormalizedHadamard (n : ℕ)
    (H : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, H i j = -1 ∨ H i j = 1) ∧
  (∀ j, H 0 j = 1) ∧
  (∀ i, H i 0 = 1) ∧
  H.transpose * H =
    ((n : ℝ) + 1) • (1 : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ)

def designIsSMatrix (n : ℕ)
    (S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ,
    designNormalizedHadamard n H ∧
    ∀ i j : Fin n, S i j = (1 - H i.succ j.succ) / 2

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
  ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
    Matrix.det A ≠ 0 →
    (∀ i j : Fin n, 0 ≤ A i j ∧ A i j ≤ 1) →
    (2 * (n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) + 1) ≤ designFrobeniusNorm n (A⁻¹)) ∧
    (designFrobeniusNorm n (A⁻¹) = 2 * (n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) + 1) ↔
      designIsSMatrix n A)

informal_statement: Let p be any prime, let m ≥ 1 be an integer, and put q = p^m. Let e ≥ 2 and r ≥ 1 be integers, let K be a finite field with exactly q^e elements, and let a be a nonzero element of K. A polynomial over K is called a permutation polynomial if its evaluation map K → K is bijective. Suppose that f(X) = X^r(X^(q−1) + a) is a permutation polynomial over K. Then there exists an integer h with 1 ≤ h < e and gcd(h,e) = 1 such that both M(X) = X^r and L(X) = X^(q^h) + aX are permutation polynomials over K, and f agrees with their composition L ∘ M as a function on K; explicitly, for every x ∈ K, x^r(x^(q−1) + a) = (x^r)^(q^h) + a x^r.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def sparseFamilyEval (K : Type*) [Field K] (q r : ℕ) (a : K) : K → K :=
  fun x => x ^ r * (x ^ (q - 1) + a)

def sparseMonomialEval (K : Type*) [Field K] (r : ℕ) : K → K :=
  fun x => x ^ r

def sparseLinearizedEval (K : Type*) [Field K] (q h : ℕ) (a : K) : K → K :=
  fun x => x ^ (q ^ h) + a * x

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (p m e r : ℕ),
  Nat.Prime p → 1 ≤ m → 2 ≤ e → 1 ≤ r →
  ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [Fintype K],
    Fintype.card K = (p ^ m) ^ e →
    ∀ (a : K), a ≠ 0 →
      Function.Bijective (sparseFamilyEval K (p ^ m) r a) →
      ∃ (h : ℕ),
        1 ≤ h ∧ h < e ∧ Nat.Coprime h e ∧
        Function.Bijective (sparseMonomialEval K r) ∧
        Function.Bijective (sparseLinearizedEval K (p ^ m) h a) ∧
        (∀ (x : K),
          sparseFamilyEval K (p ^ m) r a x =
            sparseLinearizedEval K (p ^ m) h a (sparseMonomialEval K r x))

informal_statement:
For each nonnegative integer n and each integer i with 0 ≤ i ≤ n, define the real number

d_i(n) = 4^(−n) ∑_{k=i}^n 2^k binom(2n−2k, n−k) binom(n+k, k) binom(k, i),

where binom(m,j) = m!/(j!(m−j)!) for integers 0 ≤ j ≤ m, and 0! = 1. Set d_i(n) = 0 for all integers i outside [0,n]. For a sequence a indexed by the integers, define its log-concavity transform L by (La)_i = a_i² − a_{i−1}a_{i+1}. Define L⁰a = a and L^(r+1)a = L(L^r a) for every nonnegative integer r. A nonnegative sequence is called infinitely log-concave if every entry of L^r a is nonnegative for every integer r ≥ 1. The conjecture is that, for every nonnegative integer n, the sequence (d_i(n)) indexed by the integers is infinitely log-concave; explicitly, (L^r(d(n)))_i ≥ 0 for every integer r ≥ 1 and every integer i.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable def borosMollCoefficient (n j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((4 : ℝ) ^ n)⁻¹ *
    (Finset.Icc j n).sum (fun k =>
      (2 : ℝ) ^ k *
        (Nat.choose (2 * n - 2 * k) (n - k) : ℝ) *
        (Nat.choose (n + k) k : ℝ) *
        (Nat.choose k j : ℝ))

noncomputable def borosMollSequence (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  if 0 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ (n : ℤ) then
    borosMollCoefficient n i.toNat
  else
    0

noncomputable def logConcavityTransform (a : ℤ → ℝ) : ℤ → ℝ :=
  fun i => a i ^ 2 - a (i - 1) * a (i + 1)

noncomputable def logConcavityIterate (a : ℤ → ℝ) : ℕ → (ℤ → ℝ)
  | 0 => a
  | r + 1 => logConcavityTransform (logConcavityIterate a r)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → ∀ i : ℤ,
  0 ≤ logConcavityIterate (borosMollSequence n) r i

informal_statement:
For every integer d ≥ 2 and every family of d+1 unit vectors u₁,…,u_{d+1} in ℝᵈ with its standard Euclidean inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm ‖·‖, define
M(u₁,…,u_{d+1}) = max { ‖Σ_{i=1}^{d+1} εᵢuᵢ‖² : εᵢ ∈ {−1,1} for every i }.
Then M(u₁,…,u_{d+1}) ≥ d+2, and equality holds if and only if the following condition is satisfied. There exist a positive even integer k ≤ d, a k-dimensional linear subspace E of ℝᵈ, a permutation σ of {1,…,d+1}, and signs δ₁,…,δ_{d+1} ∈ {−1,1} such that, writing wᵢ = δᵢu_{σ(i)}, the vectors w₁,…,w_{k+1} are the unit vertices of a centered regular simplex in E, and w_{k+2},…,w_{d+1} form an orthonormal basis of E⊥. Here E⊥ = {x ∈ ℝᵈ : ⟨x,y⟩ = 0 for every y ∈ E}; being the unit vertices of a centered regular simplex in E means that these vectors lie in E, span E, sum to zero, and satisfy ⟨wᵢ,wⱼ⟩ = −1/k for all distinct i,j ≤ k+1. The orthonormal basis requirement means that the remaining vectors span E⊥, have norm one, and are pairwise orthogonal; this family is empty when k=d. In particular, the minimum possible value of M over all such families is d+2.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

abbrev SignedSumSpace (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

noncomputable def signedCoefficient (b : Bool) : ℝ :=
  if b then 1 else -1

noncomputable def signedVectorSum (d : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d)
    (ε : Fin (d + 1) → Bool) : SignedSumSpace d :=
  ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), signedCoefficient (ε i) • u i

noncomputable def maximumSquaredSignedNorm (d : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d) : ℝ :=
  sSup (Set.range (fun ε : Fin (d + 1) → Bool =>
    ‖signedVectorSum d u ε‖ ^ 2))

noncomputable def simplexOrthogonalConfiguration (d : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (E : Submodule ℝ (SignedSumSpace d))
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (d + 1))) (δ : Fin (d + 1) → Bool),
    0 < k ∧ Even k ∧ k ≤ d ∧ Module.finrank ℝ E = k ∧
    (let w : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d :=
       fun i => signedCoefficient (δ i) • u (σ i)
     (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), i.val < k + 1 →
       w i ∈ E ∧ ‖w i‖ = 1) ∧
     (Submodule.span ℝ
       {v : SignedSumSpace d | ∃ i : Fin (d + 1),
         i.val < k + 1 ∧ w i = v} = E) ∧
     ((∑ i : Fin (d + 1),
       if i.val < k + 1 then w i else 0) = 0) ∧
     (∀ i j : Fin (d + 1),
       i.val < k + 1 → j.val < k + 1 → i ≠ j →
       inner ℝ (w i) (w j) = -(1 / (k : ℝ))) ∧
     (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), k + 1 ≤ i.val → ‖w i‖ = 1) ∧
     (∀ i j : Fin (d + 1),
       k + 1 ≤ i.val → k + 1 ≤ j.val → i ≠ j →
       inner ℝ (w i) (w j) = 0) ∧
     (∀ x : SignedSumSpace d,
       x ∈ Submodule.span ℝ
         {v : SignedSumSpace d | ∃ i : Fin (d + 1),
           k + 1 ≤ i.val ∧ w i = v} ↔
       ∀ y : SignedSumSpace d, y ∈ E → inner ℝ x y = 0))

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d →
  (∀ u : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d,
    (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), ‖u i‖ = 1) →
    (maximumSquaredSignedNorm d u ≥ (d : ℝ) + 2 ∧
      (maximumSquaredSignedNorm d u = (d : ℝ) + 2 ↔
        simplexOrthogonalConfiguration d u))) ∧
  (∃ u : Fin (d + 1) → SignedSumSpace d,
    (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), ‖u i‖ = 1) ∧
    maximumSquaredSignedNorm d u = (d : ℝ) + 2)

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement:
For a real number a and a nonnegative integer k, define the rising factorial by (a)₀ = 1 and (a)ₖ = ∏_{r=0}^{k−1}(a+r) when k ≥ 1. For real numbers Δ > 0 and 0 < z < 1, define the Gauss hypergeometric kernel by the convergent series
F(Δ,z) = ∑_{k=0}^∞ ((Δ)ₖ² / (2Δ)ₖ) · zᵏ/k!.
A real-valued kernel K on a product of real intervals I × J is strictly totally positive of order infinity if, for every positive integer n and every pair of strictly increasing sequences x₁ < ⋯ < xₙ in I and y₁ < ⋯ < yₙ in J, the determinant of the n × n matrix with entries K(xᵢ,yⱼ) is strictly positive.
The conjecture is that F is strictly totally positive of order infinity on (0,∞) × (0,1). Explicitly, for every positive integer n, all real numbers 0 < Δ₁ < ⋯ < Δₙ, and all real numbers 0 < z₁ < ⋯ < zₙ < 1, one has det[F(Δᵢ,zⱼ)]_{i,j=1}^n > 0.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable def realRisingProduct (a : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (Finset.range k).prod (fun r => a + (r : ℝ))

noncomputable def gaussDiagonalKernel (Δ z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑' k : ℕ,
    (realRisingProduct Δ k) ^ 2 / realRisingProduct (2 * Δ) k *
      z ^ k / (Nat.factorial k : ℝ)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n →
  ∀ (Δ z : Fin n → ℝ),
    StrictMono Δ →
    StrictMono z →
    (∀ i : Fin n, 0 < Δ i) →
    (∀ j : Fin n, 0 < z j ∧ z j < 1) →
    0 < Matrix.det (fun i j : Fin n => gaussDiagonalKernel (Δ i) (z j))

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement:
All graphs below are finite, undirected, and have no loops or parallel edges. For a graph G and a vertex subset X, G[X] denotes the graph on X containing exactly those edges of G whose endpoints both lie in X. A vertex set is independent if no two of its vertices are adjacent. An induced matching in G is a collection of edges with pairwise distinct endpoints such that the graph induced by all their endpoints contains exactly the selected edges.

For a positive integer r, an r-obstruction is any graph F whose vertex set has a partition into four independent sets A, B, C, D, each of cardinality r, such that F[A ∪ B] and F[C ∪ D] each consist of exactly r disjoint edges, and every vertex of B is adjacent to every vertex of C. No restrictions are imposed on edges between A and C, between A and D, or between B and D. A graph excludes r-obstructions as induced subgraphs if none of its induced subgraphs is isomorphic to any r-obstruction.

A tree decomposition of G consists of a finite nonempty tree T and a vertex subset β(t) of G for each node t of T, called its bag, satisfying: every vertex of G belongs to a bag; both endpoints of every edge of G belong to a common bag; and, for each vertex v of G, the nodes whose bags contain v induce a connected subtree of T. The induced matching cost of a bag B is the largest cardinality of an induced matching in G such that every selected edge has at least one endpoint in B. The edges need not have both endpoints in B. The induced matching treewidth of G is the minimum, over all its tree decompositions, of the maximum induced matching cost of a bag.

For a graph G with at least two vertices, a branch decomposition consists of a finite tree T in which every node has degree at most three, together with a bijection δ from the vertices of G to the leaves of T. Deleting an edge e of T divides its leaves into two parts and therefore gives a partition (S_e, V(G) \ S_e) of the vertices of G. The cut value at e is the largest cardinality of an induced matching in G whose every edge has one endpoint in each part of this partition. The sim-width of the branch decomposition is the maximum of these cut values, and the sim-width of G is their minimum over all branch decompositions. Set the sim-width of graphs with at most one vertex to zero.

A class of graphs has a bounded parameter if there exists a nonnegative integer that bounds that parameter for every graph in the class. Is it true that, for every positive integer r, every class of graphs with bounded sim-width that excludes r-obstructions as induced subgraphs has bounded induced matching treewidth? No closure assumption on the graph class is imposed.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def GraphWidthPath {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (a b : Fin m) (l : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Fin m) : Prop :=
  p 0 = a ∧ p l = b ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l → T.Adj (p i) (p (i + 1))) ∧
  (∀ i j : ℕ, i ≤ l → j ≤ l → p i = p j → i = j)

def GraphWidthTree {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : Fin m,
    ∃ (l : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Fin m),
      GraphWidthPath T a b l p ∧
      (∀ (l' : ℕ) (p' : ℕ → Fin m),
        GraphWidthPath T a b l' p' →
        l' = l ∧ (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l → p' i = p i))

def GraphWidthSubcubic {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (t : Fin m) (f : Fin 4 → Fin m),
    (∀ i : Fin 4, T.Adj t (f i)) → ¬ Function.Injective f

def GraphWidthLeaf {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (t : Fin m) : Prop :=
  ∃ u : Fin m, T.Adj t u ∧
    (∀ v : Fin m, T.Adj t v → v = u)

def GraphWidthReachDeleting {m : ℕ} (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (a b u v : Fin m) : Prop :=
  ∃ (l : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Fin m),
    GraphWidthPath T u v l p ∧
    (∀ i : ℕ, i < l →
      ¬ ((p i = a ∧ p (i + 1) = b) ∨
         (p i = b ∧ p (i + 1) = a)))

def GraphWidthInducedMatching {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (q : ℕ) (x y : Fin q → Fin n) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective (Sum.elim x y) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin q, G.Adj (x i) (y i)) ∧
  (∀ i j : Fin q, i ≠ j →
    ¬ G.Adj (x i) (x j) ∧
    ¬ G.Adj (x i) (y j) ∧
    ¬ G.Adj (y i) (x j) ∧
    ¬ G.Adj (y i) (y j))

def GraphWidthTreeDecomposition {n m : ℕ}
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
    (bag : Fin m → Set (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  0 < m ∧ GraphWidthTree T ∧
  (∀ v : Fin n, ∃ t : Fin m, v ∈ bag t) ∧
  (∀ u v : Fin n, G.Adj u v →
    ∃ t : Fin m, u ∈ bag t ∧ v ∈ bag t) ∧
  (∀ (v : Fin n) (a b : Fin m),
    v ∈ bag a → v ∈ bag b →
    ∃ (l : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Fin m),
      GraphWidthPath T a b l p ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l → v ∈ bag (p i)))

def GraphWidthMatchingTreewidthAtMost {n : ℕ}
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m))
      (bag : Fin m → Set (Fin n)),
    GraphWidthTreeDecomposition G T bag ∧
    (∀ (t : Fin m) (q : ℕ) (x y : Fin q → Fin n),
      GraphWidthInducedMatching G q x y →
      (∀ i : Fin q, x i ∈ bag t ∨ y i ∈ bag t) →
      q ≤ k)

def GraphWidthSimAtMost {n : ℕ}
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  n ≤ 1 ∨
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (δ : Fin n → Fin m),
    0 < m ∧ GraphWidthTree T ∧ GraphWidthSubcubic T ∧
    Function.Injective δ ∧
    (∀ t : Fin m, GraphWidthLeaf T t ↔
      ∃ v : Fin n, δ v = t) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin m, T.Adj a b →
      ∀ (q : ℕ) (x y : Fin q → Fin n),
        GraphWidthInducedMatching G q x y →
        (∀ i : Fin q,
          GraphWidthReachDeleting T a b (δ (x i)) a ∧
          ¬ GraphWidthReachDeleting T a b (δ (y i)) a) →
        q ≤ s)

def GraphWidthContainsObstruction {n : ℕ}
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Fin r × Fin 4 → Fin n,
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ (i j : Fin r) (c : Fin 4),
      ¬ G.Adj (f (i, c)) (f (j, c))) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin r,
      (G.Adj (f (i, 0)) (f (j, 1)) ↔ i = j) ∧
      (G.Adj (f (i, 2)) (f (j, 3)) ↔ i = j)) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin r, G.Adj (f (i, 1)) (f (j, 2)))

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r →
  ∀ C : (n : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin n) → Prop,
    (∃ s : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      C n G → GraphWidthSimAtMost G s) →
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      C n G → ¬ GraphWidthContainsObstruction G r) →
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      C n G → GraphWidthMatchingTreewidthAtMost G k

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement: For each integer n ≥ 3, let Q_n be the finite simple undirected graph with vertex set {−1,1}^n, in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when they differ in one coordinate. For a function f : {−1,1}^n → ℝ, define its graph Laplacian by (L_{Q_n}f)(x) = ∑_{y adjacent to x}(f(x) − f(y)). A Laplacian eigenfunction with eigenvalue λ is a function f that is not identically zero and satisfies (L_{Q_n}f)(x) = λf(x) at every vertex x. Define S_+(f) = {x : f(x) > 0} and S_−(f) = {x : f(x) < 0}. The strong nodal domains of f are the connected components of the subgraph induced by S_+(f), together with the connected components of the subgraph induced by S_−(f); vertices where f vanishes belong to neither subgraph. For every integer n ≥ 3 and every integer i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 2, there exists a Laplacian eigenfunction on Q_n with eigenvalue 2i and exactly two strong nodal domains.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

abbrev CubeVertex (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Bool

def CubeAdjacent {n : ℕ} (x y : CubeVertex n) : Prop :=
  ∃ j : Fin n, x j ≠ y j ∧
    ∀ k : Fin n, k ≠ j → x k = y k

noncomputable def CubeLaplacian {n : ℕ}
    (f : CubeVertex n → ℝ) (x : CubeVertex n) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ y : CubeVertex n,
    if CubeAdjacent x y then f x - f y else 0

def CubeStrongStep {n : ℕ} (f : CubeVertex n → ℝ)
    (x y : CubeVertex n) : Prop :=
  CubeAdjacent x y ∧
    ((0 < f x ∧ 0 < f y) ∨ (f x < 0 ∧ f y < 0))

def CubeSameStrongDomain {n : ℕ} (f : CubeVertex n → ℝ)
    (x y : CubeVertex n) : Prop :=
  f x ≠ 0 ∧ f y ≠ 0 ∧
    Relation.ReflTransGen (CubeStrongStep f) x y

def CubeHasTwoStrongDomains {n : ℕ}
    (f : CubeVertex n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x y : CubeVertex n,
    f x ≠ 0 ∧ f y ≠ 0 ∧
    ¬ CubeSameStrongDomain f x y ∧
    ∀ z : CubeVertex n, f z ≠ 0 →
      CubeSameStrongDomain f z x ∨ CubeSameStrongDomain f z y

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n - 2 →
  ∃ f : CubeVertex n → ℝ,
    (∃ x : CubeVertex n, f x ≠ 0) ∧
    (∀ x : CubeVertex n,
      CubeLaplacian f x = ((2 : ℝ) * (i : ℝ)) * f x) ∧
    CubeHasTwoStrongDomains f

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement: Let V be the set of all one-dimensional linear subspaces of the Euclidean space ℝ³. Define a graph G with vertex set V by declaring distinct L,M ∈ V adjacent exactly when u·v = 0 for every u ∈ L and v ∈ M, where · is the Euclidean inner product. Let S¹ = {z ∈ ℝ² : ‖z‖₂ = 1}. For a,b ∈ S¹, define d(a,b) = arccos(a·b) ∈ [0,π], the length of the shorter arc between a and b on the unit circle. Define the circular chromatic number χ_c(G) to be the infimum of the real numbers r ≥ 1 for which there exists a function f:V → S¹ satisfying d(f(L),f(M)) ≥ 2π/r for every adjacent pair L,M. No continuity, measurability, or other regularity is required of f; the infimum of an empty set is understood to be +∞. The conjecture is that χ_c(G) = 4.

Let n be any nonnegative integer, and let G be any finite simple graph with ordered vertex set {1,...,2n}. A perfect matching of G is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges covering every vertex; write M(G) for the set of perfect matchings. Associate a distinct commuting indeterminate x_e to each edge e, and define the perfect-matching polynomial over the real numbers by PM(G) = Σ_{M∈M(G)} ∏_{e∈M} x_e. An orientation D of G chooses one direction for each edge. For a perfect matching M, enumerate its edges as u_1v_1,...,u_nv_n, with each edge directed from u_i to v_i in D. Let s_D(M) be the sign of the permutation whose sequence of values is (u_1,v_1,...,u_n,v_n). This sign is independent of the enumeration of the matching edges. Define the oriented Pfaffian polynomial by Pf_D(G) = Σ_{M∈M(G)} s_D(M) ∏_{e∈M} x_e. Empty products and the sign of the empty permutation are 1. The Pfaffian number pf(G) is the least positive integer k for which there exist orientations D_1,...,D_k of G and real numbers c_1,...,c_k such that PM(G) = Σ_{i=1}^k c_i Pf_{D_i}(G) as an identity of polynomials. Is it true that, for every such G, if pf(G) > 1, then pf(G) is even?
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def pfPairFirst (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : Fin (2 * n) :=
  ⟨2 * i.val, by omega⟩

def pfPairSecond (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : Fin (2 * n) :=
  ⟨2 * i.val + 1, by omega⟩

def pfMatchingEncoding (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n)))
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : Fin n, G.Adj (σ (pfPairFirst n i)) (σ (pfPairSecond n i))

def pfOrientation (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))) :=
  {d : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → Bool //
    ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → (d u v = true ↔ d v u = false)}

noncomputable def pfMatchingSign (n : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))) (D : pfOrientation n G)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * n))) : ℝ :=
  (((Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤˣ) : ℤ) : ℝ) *
    ∏ i : Fin n,
      (if D.1 (σ (pfPairFirst n i)) (σ (pfPairSecond n i)) = true
       then (1 : ℝ) else -1)

def pfRepresentation (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n)))
    (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ D : Fin k → pfOrientation n G,
    ∃ c : Fin k → ℝ,
      ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (2 * n)),
        pfMatchingEncoding n G σ →
          (∑ t : Fin k, c t * pfMatchingSign n G (D t) σ) = 1

def pfHasNumber (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n)))
    (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  0 < k ∧ pfRepresentation n G k ∧
    ∀ l : ℕ, 0 < l → pfRepresentation n G l → k ≤ l

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n))) (k : ℕ), pfHasNumber n G k → 1 < k → Even k

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement:
For every integer n ≥ 4, every integer k ≥ 1, and every collection of integers q_ij ≥ 2 indexed by 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, make the following construction. A labeled quiver on [n] = {1,…,n} is a finite directed graph with these vertex labels, allowing parallel arrows but having no loops or oriented 2-cycles. Represent it by its skew-symmetric integer matrix B, where B_ij is the number of arrows i → j minus the number of arrows j → i. Equality of quivers means equality of these matrices, without relabeling.

For a matrix B and a vertex v, define mutation μ_v(B) by B'_ij = −B_ij if i = v or j = v, and otherwise by B'_ij = B_ij + [B_iv]_+[B_vj]_+ − [−B_iv]_+[−B_vj]_+, where [x]_+ = max(x,0). A mutation word (i_1,…,i_s) acts from left to right, so μ_(i_1,…,i_s) = μ_i_s ∘ ⋯ ∘ μ_i_1. Write (a,b)^k for k repetitions of the two-term word (a,b), and concatenate displayed words in their written order.

Let R be the quiver on [n−1] whose matrix satisfies R_ij = q_ij for i < j. Define a quiver X on [n] by requiring its matrix restricted to [n−1] × [n−1] to be μ_(2,1)^k(R), and requiring X_in = q_in for every i < n; diagonal and lower-triangular entries are determined by skew-symmetry. Starting at X, consider the word W = (n)(1,2)^k(n−1,n−2,…,1)(2,1)^k, which has length n+4k, and its successive mutated quivers.

The mutation class of X consists of all labeled quivers obtained from X by finite mutation words. Its labeled mutation graph has these quivers as vertices, with an undirected edge labeled v between Y and μ_v(Y). A mutation cycle is a closed walk of positive length in this graph with no stationary step and with consecutive edge labels distinct, including the last and first labels. Such a cycle is simple when its quiver vertices are pairwise distinct except for the equality of the final and initial vertex. Cycles are identified only by changing the starting position or reversing traversal, not by relabeling quiver vertices.

The conjecture is that the walk prescribed by W is the unique simple mutation cycle in the labeled mutation graph of the mutation class of X.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def MutationMatrix (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Fin n → ℤ

def IsMutationQuiver {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, B i j = -B j i

def MutateMatrix {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n) (v : ℕ) : MutationMatrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    if i.val = v ∨ j.val = v then -B i j
    else
      B i j +
        (∑ a : Fin n, if a.val = v then
          max (B i a) 0 * max (B a j) 0 -
          max (-B i a) 0 * max (-B a j) 0
        else 0)

def ApplyMutationWord {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n)
    (w : List ℕ) : MutationMatrix n :=
  w.foldl (fun C v => MutateMatrix C v) B

def ValidMutationWord (n : ℕ) (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v ∈ w, v < n

def AlternatingMutationWord (a b : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ
  | 0 => []
  | k + 1 => a :: b :: AlternatingMutationWord a b k

def ReferenceMutationMatrix (n : ℕ) (q : MutationMatrix n) : MutationMatrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    if i.val + 1 < n ∧ j.val + 1 < n then
      if i.val < j.val then q i j
      else if j.val < i.val then -q j i
      else 0
    else 0

def InitialMutationMatrix (n k : ℕ) (q : MutationMatrix n) : MutationMatrix n :=
  let C := ApplyMutationWord (ReferenceMutationMatrix n q)
    (AlternatingMutationWord 1 0 k)
  fun i j =>
    if i = j then 0
    else if j.val + 1 = n then q i j
    else if i.val + 1 = n then -q j i
    else C i j

def PrescribedMutationWord (n k : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  [n - 1] ++ AlternatingMutationWord 0 1 k ++
    (List.range (n - 1)).reverse ++ AlternatingMutationWord 1 0 k

def MutationState {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n)
    (w : List ℕ) (t : ℕ) : MutationMatrix n :=
  ApplyMutationWord B (w.take t)

def MutationReachable {n : ℕ} (B C : MutationMatrix n) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : List ℕ, ValidMutationWord n w ∧ ApplyMutationWord B w = C

def IsSimpleMutationCycle {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n)
    (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsMutationQuiver B ∧
  0 < w.length ∧
  ValidMutationWord n w ∧
  ApplyMutationWord B w = B ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, t < w.length →
    MutationState B w t ≠ MutationState B w (t + 1)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, t < w.length →
    w.getD t 0 ≠ w.getD ((t + 1) % w.length) 0) ∧
  (∀ s t : ℕ, s < w.length → t < w.length →
    MutationState B w s = MutationState B w t → s = t)

def SameMutationCycle {n : ℕ} (B : MutationMatrix n) (u : List ℕ)
    (C : MutationMatrix n) (w : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  w.length = u.length ∧
  ∃ s : ℕ, s < u.length ∧ C = MutationState B u s ∧
    ((∀ j : ℕ, j < u.length →
        w.getD j 0 = u.getD ((s + j) % u.length) 0) ∨
     (∀ j : ℕ, j < u.length →
        w.getD j 0 = u.getD ((s + u.length - 1 - j) % u.length) 0))

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n k : ℕ) (q : MutationMatrix n),
  4 ≤ n → 1 ≤ k →
  (∀ i j : Fin n, i.val < j.val → (2 : ℤ) ≤ q i j) →
  let X := InitialMutationMatrix n k q
  let W := PrescribedMutationWord n k
  IsSimpleMutationCycle X W ∧
    ∀ (Y : MutationMatrix n) (w : List ℕ),
      MutationReachable X Y → IsSimpleMutationCycle Y w →
        SameMutationCycle X W Y w

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement:
Let ℕ₊={1,2,3,…}. For a real number p with 1<p<2 and a real sequence y:ℕ₊→ℝ, define ‖y‖ₚ=(∑_{n=1}^∞ |y(n)|^p)^{1/p}, with value +∞ if the sum diverges, and define ℓ^p(ℕ₊)={y:‖y‖ₚ<∞}. Let Dₚ be the cone of sequences x∈ℓ^p(ℕ₊) such that x(n)≥0 and x(n+1)≤x(n) for every n≥1. Define the Copson operator on ℓ^p(ℕ₊) by (C*x)(n)=∑_{k=n}^∞ x(k)/k; these series converge absolutely for p>1. Let I be the identity operator, so ((C*−I)x)(n)=(C*x)(n)−x(n). Define its norm restricted to Dₚ by Nₚ=sup{‖(C*−I)x‖ₚ/‖x‖ₚ : x∈Dₚ, x≠0}, where the supremum is allowed to be +∞. Is it true that, for every real p with 1<p<2,
Nₚ=(∫_{(0,1)} |ln t+1|^p dt)^{1/p},
where ln is the natural logarithm and the integral is with respect to Lebesgue measure?
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped ENNReal BigOperators

noncomputable def sequencePNorm (p : ℝ) (x : ℕ → ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ENNReal.rpow
    (∑' n : ℕ, ENNReal.rpow (ENNReal.ofReal (|x n|)) p)
    (1 / p)

def decreasingLpCone (p : ℝ) (x : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  sequencePNorm p x < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ x n) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, x (n + 1) ≤ x n)

noncomputable def copsonPositiveTail (x : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ENNReal :=
  ∑' j : ℕ, ENNReal.ofReal
    (x (n + j) / ((n + j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))

noncomputable def copsonIdentityMagnitude (x : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ENNReal :=
  (copsonPositiveTail x n - ENNReal.ofReal (x n)) +
  (ENNReal.ofReal (x n) - copsonPositiveTail x n)

noncomputable def copsonIdentityPNorm (p : ℝ) (x : ℕ → ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ENNReal.rpow
    (∑' n : ℕ, ENNReal.rpow (copsonIdentityMagnitude x n) p)
    (1 / p)

noncomputable def restrictedCopsonIdentityNorm (p : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  sSup {r : ENNReal | ∃ x : ℕ → ℝ,
    decreasingLpCone p x ∧
    x ≠ (fun _ : ℕ => (0 : ℝ)) ∧
    r = copsonIdentityPNorm p x / sequencePNorm p x}

noncomputable def logarithmicIntegralPNorm (p : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ENNReal.rpow
    (∫⁻ t in Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1,
      ENNReal.rpow (ENNReal.ofReal (|Real.log t + 1|)) p)
    (1 / p)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p → p < 2 →
  restrictedCopsonIdentityNorm p = logarithmicIntegralPNorm p

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement: For every integer n ≥ 6, every finite set V with |V| = n, and every indexed family (G₁, …, Gₙ) of simple undirected graphs on V, with repetitions allowed, suppose that |E(Gᵢ)| ≥ (n−1)(n−2)/2 + 1 for every i ∈ {1, …, n}. Here a simple undirected graph on V has an edge set consisting of unordered pairs of distinct elements of V. Define Hₙ to be the graph obtained from a complete graph on n−1 vertices by adjoining one new vertex and exactly one edge joining that new vertex to one of the original vertices; a complete graph contains every unordered pair of distinct vertices as an edge. Graphs are isomorphic if there is a bijection between their vertex sets that preserves adjacency in both directions. If it is not the case that G₁ = ⋯ = Gₙ as graphs on V and their common graph is isomorphic to Hₙ, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian cycle in the family. Explicitly, there exist an ordering v₀, …, vₙ₋₁ of all vertices of V and a bijection c : {0, …, n−1} → {1, …, n} such that {vⱼ, v₍ⱼ₊₁₎ mod n} ∈ E(G_{c(j)}) for every j ∈ {0, …, n−1}.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable def collectionEdgeCount {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  Set.ncard G.edgeSet

def collectionCycleNext {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (j : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ⟨(j.val + 1) % n, Nat.mod_lt (j.val + 1) hn⟩

def collectionRainbowHamiltonian {n : ℕ} {V : Type}
    (G : Fin n → SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (hn : 0 < n) (v : Fin n ≃ V) (c : Fin n ≃ Fin n),
    ∀ j : Fin n,
      (G (c j)).Adj (v j) (v (collectionCycleNext hn j))

def collectionCommonPendantClique {n : ℕ} {V : Type}
    (G : Fin n → SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (v u : V), v ≠ u ∧
    ∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : V),
      (G i).Adj x y ↔
        x ≠ y ∧
          ((x ≠ v ∧ y ≠ v) ∨
           (x = v ∧ y = u) ∨
           (x = u ∧ y = v))

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ), 6 ≤ n →
  ∀ (V : Type) (inst : Fintype V),
    @Fintype.card V inst = n →
    ∀ (G : Fin n → SimpleGraph V),
      (∀ i : Fin n, Nat.choose (n - 1) 2 + 1 ≤ collectionEdgeCount (G i)) →
      ¬ collectionCommonPendantClique G →
      collectionRainbowHamiltonian G

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement:
A finite nonempty partially ordered set T is a tree poset if the following undirected graph is a tree (connected and without cycles): its vertices are the elements of T, and u and v are adjacent precisely when one covers the other. Here v covers u if u < v and there is no w with u < w < v. Let h(T) be the maximum cardinality of a chain in T, where a chain is a subset whose elements are pairwise comparable.

Define the rooted b-blow-up T(x,b), for x ∈ T and an integer b ≥ 2, as follows. Root the undirected cover graph at x, and let d(x,u) be the number of edges on its unique path from x to u. Replace each u by vertices (u,a), where a is a word of length d(x,u) over the alphabet {1,…,b}; thus x has one replacement vertex, indexed by the empty word. For each cover-graph edge with parent v and child u relative to this root, join (v,a) to (u,ai) for every word a of length d(x,v) and every i ∈ {1,…,b}, where ai denotes appending i to a. Orient each such edge in the same order direction as the original edge: from the replacement of the smaller element of T to the replacement of the larger element. The order on T(x,b) is the reflexive transitive closure of these directed edges.

For a positive integer n, write [n] = {1,…,n}, and let 2^[n] be its power set. A family F ⊆ 2^[n] contains a weak copy of a finite poset Q if there is an injective map f : Q → F such that p ≤ q implies f(p) ⊆ f(q); no condition is imposed on images of incomparable elements.

For every tree poset T and every real ε > 0, there exist a real δ > 0 and a positive integer n₀, depending only on T and ε, such that for every integer n ≥ n₀, every x ∈ T, and every family F ⊆ 2^[n] satisfying
|F| ≥ (h(T) − 1 + ε) · binomial(n, floor(n/2)),
the family F contains a weak copy of T(x, floor(δn)). The threshold n₀ is understood to be large enough that floor(δn) ≥ 2 for all n ≥ n₀.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

def TreeCover (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)) (u v : Fin m) : Prop :=
  letI := P
  u < v ∧ ¬ ∃ w : Fin m, u < w ∧ w < v

def TreeAdjacent (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)) (u v : Fin m) : Prop :=
  TreeCover m P u v ∨ TreeCover m P v u

inductive TreeWalk (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)) :
    Fin m → Fin m → List (Fin m) → Prop where
  | nil (u : Fin m) : TreeWalk m P u u []
  | cons {u w v : Fin m} {p : List (Fin m)} :
      TreeAdjacent m P u w → TreeWalk m P w v p →
      TreeWalk m P u v (w :: p)

def IsTreePoset (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)) : Prop :=
  0 < m ∧ ∀ u v : Fin m,
    ∃! p : List (Fin m), TreeWalk m P u v p ∧ (u :: p).Nodup

noncomputable def TreeDistance (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m))
    (u v : Fin m) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ p : List (Fin m), TreeWalk m P u v p ∧ (u :: p).Nodup
    then (Classical.choose h).length
    else 0

noncomputable def TreeHeight (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)) : ℕ := by
  classical
  letI := P
  exact (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin m))).sup
    (fun s => if (∀ u ∈ s, ∀ v ∈ s, u ≤ v ∨ v ≤ u) then s.card else 0)

def RootedVertices (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m))
    (x : Fin m) (b : ℕ) : Type :=
  Σ u : Fin m, {a : List (Fin b) // a.length = TreeDistance m P x u}

def RootedEdge (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m))
    (x : Fin m) (b : ℕ)
    (p q : RootedVertices m P x b) : Prop :=
  TreeCover m P p.1 q.1 ∧
    ((TreeDistance m P x q.1 = TreeDistance m P x p.1 + 1 ∧
        ∃ i : Fin b, q.2.val = p.2.val ++ [i]) ∨
     (TreeDistance m P x p.1 = TreeDistance m P x q.1 + 1 ∧
        ∃ i : Fin b, p.2.val = q.2.val ++ [i]))

def RootedOrder (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m))
    (x : Fin m) (b : ℕ)
    (p q : RootedVertices m P x b) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (RootedEdge m P x b) p q

def ContainsRootedCopy (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m))
    (x : Fin m) (b n : ℕ) (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : RootedVertices m P x b → Finset (Fin n),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ p, f p ∈ F) ∧
    (∀ p q, RootedOrder m P x b p q → f p ⊆ f q)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ (m : ℕ) (P : PartialOrder (Fin m)), IsTreePoset m P →
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∃ (δ : ℝ) (n₀ : ℕ),
      0 < δ ∧ 0 < n₀ ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → 2 ≤ ⌊δ * (n : ℝ)⌋₊) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
        ∀ (x : Fin m) (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
          (F.card : ℝ) ≥
            ((TreeHeight m P : ℝ) - 1 + ε) *
              (Nat.choose n (n / 2) : ℝ) →
          ContainsRootedCopy m P x ⌊δ * (n : ℝ)⌋₊ n F)

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry

informal_statement: For every positive integer n, let [n] = {1,…,n} and let Ω be the set of all subsets of [n], ordered by inclusion. For x ∈ Ω, write x̄ = [n] \ x and x_i = 1 if i ∈ x and x_i = 0 otherwise. Let h : Ω → ℝ be increasing, meaning that h(x) ≤ h(y) whenever x ⊆ y, and antipodal, meaning that h(x̄) = −h(x) for every x ∈ Ω. Define h₊(x) = max{h(x),0}. For every S ⊆ [n], define the Fourier coefficient ĥ(S) = 2^(−n) ∑_{x∈Ω} h(x)(−1)^{|S∩x|}. For every nonempty T ⊆ [n] and every i ∈ T, choose a real number λ_T(i) ≥ 0, subject to ∑_{i∈T} λ_T(i) = ĥ(T)^2. Define λ_i = ∑_{T⊆[n], i∈T} λ_T(i) and L_λ(x) = ∑_{i=1}^n λ_i x_i. Then there exists a function β : Ω × Ω → ℝ with β(x,y) ≥ 0 for all x,y, with β(x,y) = 0 whenever x ⊈ y, and with the marginals ∑_{y∈Ω} β(x,y) = L_λ(x) for every x ∈ Ω and ∑_{x∈Ω} β(x,y) = h₊(y)^2 for every y ∈ Ω.
formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable def cubeFourier (n : ℕ)
    (h : Finset (Fin n) → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (∑ x : Finset (Fin n), h x * (-1 : ℝ) ^ (S ∩ x).card) /
    (2 : ℝ) ^ n

noncomputable def cubeCoordinateWeight (n : ℕ)
    (lam : Finset (Fin n) → Fin n → ℝ) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ T : Finset (Fin n), if i ∈ T then lam T i else 0

noncomputable def cubeLinearWeight (n : ℕ)
    (lam : Finset (Fin n) → Fin n → ℝ) (x : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, cubeCoordinateWeight n lam i *
    (if i ∈ x then (1 : ℝ) else 0)

def cubePositiveSquare (n : ℕ)
    (h : Finset (Fin n) → ℝ) (x : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  (max (h x) 0) ^ 2

def cubeUpwardFlow (n : ℕ)
    (p q : Finset (Fin n) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ beta : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) → ℝ,
    (∀ x y, 0 ≤ beta x y) ∧
    (∀ x y, ¬ x ⊆ y → beta x y = 0) ∧
    (∀ x, (∑ y : Finset (Fin n), beta x y) = p x) ∧
    (∀ y, (∑ x : Finset (Fin n), beta x y) = q y)

def arxivleanConjecture : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
  ∀ (h : Finset (Fin n) → ℝ)
    (lam : Finset (Fin n) → Fin n → ℝ),
    (∀ x y : Finset (Fin n), x ⊆ y → h x ≤ h y) →
    (∀ x : Finset (Fin n), h (Finset.univ \ x) = -h x) →
    (∀ T : Finset (Fin n), T.Nonempty →
      (∀ i : Fin n, i ∈ T → 0 ≤ lam T i) ∧
      (∑ i ∈ T, lam T i) = (cubeFourier n h T) ^ 2) →
    cubeUpwardFlow n (cubeLinearWeight n lam) (cubePositiveSquare n h)

theorem arxivlean : arxivleanConjecture := by sorry
